Deportation (EJ): on June 16 1944 Jews were transferred to the Szeged ghetto; from there 378 deported to Auschwitz and 500 to Wiener-Neustadt and other places in Austria. Deportation counts, not a resident population.

KehilaLinks table: 831 (in 428 families). Further: on June 16 1944 737 Jews were herded into the synagogue; deported June 25-28 to Auschwitz and Wiener-Neustadt; of those sent to Auschwitz only five returned (deportation/survivor counts, not population).

Report by Orsai Antal dated May 19 1944: 428 Israelite families, 831 Israelite persons (of whom 16 interned, 94 in labour service); plus 34 Christian-religion Jews and 55 in mixed marriages. Community's own list of April 8 1944 gave 826.
June 1944: 737 Jews transported from Hódmezővásárhely to Szeged by rail (railway billing record). Deportation count, not population.

Deportation began June 16 1944; almost 750 people reached Szeged on the 19th; the city set up no ghetto thanks to deputy mayor Pál Beretzk. About 400 Hódmezővásárhely victims of the Holocaust (deportation/death counts).
Concentration June 16 1944 and deportation of about 800 people from June 17 to the Szeged brickworks transit ghetto; about 400 perished (deportation/victim counts).
During the Holocaust Hódmezővásárhely was the only town in Hungary whose authorities set up no ghetto despite government orders.

Pre-deportation local Jewish population 'did not reach nine hundred' (upper bound, undated beyond 1944 context); ghettoization began June 16 1944, taken to Szeged then Strasshof on June 25/27/28.
